reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend helpers, although occurrence filtering and adjustment remain repeated across consumers.

duplication.why: The two server handlers duplicate rule construction and the filter-and-adjust pipeline, which also overlaps with getNextDate.

placement.why: Holiday matching and date adjustment belong in shared/schedules.ts, but the server handlers retain part of the occurrence-selection policy.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the four requested schedule changes, their consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The small shared predicates are understandable, but maintainers must coordinate several filtering pipelines and frequency-dependent behavior across the adjustment helpers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed consumers use the existing recurrence and weekend abstractions, extended with shared holiday and daily-skip predicates.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts expresses daily off-day filtering through isKept and firstOccurrence, while server/schedules/app.ts expresses the same selection through dropWeekends and inline continue branches.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter, and applyWeekendRule plus applyWeekendRuleToDay gain daily-frequency exceptions; consumers still call the shared helpers.
